messages:
lia: heads up — acme reported ~20 users lost roles after an SSO/SCIM sync at 3pm UTC. they say group membership still shows on their IdP but role mappings in our console are missing. any guesses?

sam: thanks lia. can you paste the original SCIM PATCH we received and the response from the /v1/scim/users endpoint? suspecting externalId mismatch or scope issue. cc @marco for provisioning logic.

lia: pasted below (redacted):
```
PATCH /scim/v2/Users/3a2b1c
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
{
  "Operations": [
    {"op": "replace", "path": "members", "value": [{"value": "urn:okta:user:12345"}, {"value": "urn:okta:user:23456"}]}
  ]
}
```

sam: response was 200 but token scope on the connector shows `scim:read` only — that would allow reads but not update role links. can you confirm the connector token scopes from the IdP app?

lia: i pulled the connector log. token scope list: `[scim:read, scim:groups]` — no `scim:write`. customer claims they never changed it.

marco: hmm. missing write scope would block role assignment updates, but shouldn't cause existing roles to drop. can you check if our onboarding flow normalized externalIds? i.e. our SCIM normalization that strips suffixes like `@okta` was recently toggled. if IdP sends `externalId: acct-12345.okta` and we stored `acct-12345`, that could create a shadowed identity when SSO links later with full suffix.

lia: good point. i see an entry in the provisioning audit: `externalId_normalize: true` was applied during a bulk import last month. customer did an SSO link yesterday which created new identities with full externalId (suffix included) and then SCIM resync removed the old mappings.

julie: action items — short repro steps for eng: 1) reproduce with a sample org creating users via bulk import (normalize=true) then link an SSO account that sends full externalId. 2) run a SCIM group PATCH that references the full externalId and observe role drop. 3) capture `GET /scim/v2/Users?filter=externalId eq "acct-12345.okta"` vs `acct-12345`.

sam: repro attempt notes: i simulated locally. when `externalId_normalize=true`, we store `acct-12345`. later SSO-provisioned user with externalId `acct-12345.okta` results in a new internal user record, and the old user is orphaned. group-to-role mapping still attached to the orphaned internal id, so the visible role set on the linked user is empty.

marco: thanks. proposed customer-facing mitigation: run a one-off migration: for each orphaned internal user where `externalId_normalize=true`, add a canonical alias mapping from normalized -> full-suffix externalId, or run a backfill that merges records. also request the IdP admin to add `scim:write` scope to the connector token so future PATCHes won't silently fail.

lia: i've sent the customer interim steps: 1) add `scim:write` to the connector app, 2) hold off on bulk imports, 3) we can run a scoped backfill (need eng approval). they responded :thumbsup:.

scim-bot: incident-tracker created (INC-2026) — label: scim-externalid-normalize. assigned to eng-provisioning.

julie: next — eng PR will add a safety when `externalId_normalize` is enabled: create a suffix-preserving alias table and log potential duplicates on import. marco, can you open the PR?

marco: on it, i'll include unit tests and a migration plan. ETA EOD tomorrow.

lia: thanks team, marking this resolved for CS pending the backfill. i'll update the customer after the migration is scheduled.
